clue.text: Drink toasts, perhaps — all abroad

parts.note: to toast bread is one way to brown it, so toasts is an example of browns
tout is the French word for all, so all as said abroad

explanation.surface: Someone raises toasts at a drinks party where everyone is overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abroad' tells you to translate 'all' into French. Brown stout is an old name for a dark porter-style beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown stout is a dark, strong beer, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Brook gives score Len put up

parts.note: in cricket a run is a score

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up means the name Len is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: the name taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricketer called Len makes a score beside a stream.
explanation.definitionFit: A runnel is a small stream or rivulet, the same thing as a brook.

clue.text: Bird has a job to carry load, perhaps

indicators.note: one word carrying another holds it inside, so the job wraps round the other letters

parts.note: a job is work

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word load may be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A labourer's task is to haul a heavy load.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To carry' puts ODLA (a rearrangement of LOAD, signalled by 'perhaps') inside WORK.
explanation.definitionFit: The woodlark is a small songbird of the lark family.

clue.text: Curses when clothing falls between hangers

indicators.note: one piece dropping between parts of another sits inside it

parts.note: a hanger is an old word for a short sword hung from the belt
wear is clothing, as in menswear

explanation.surface: Someone swears as their clothes slip down between the coat hangers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hangers' looks like wardrobe gear, but a hanger is also a short sword; WEAR goes between S and WORDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Curses are oaths or profanities, which is what swear words are.

clue.text: No-one turns up to fill new, post, finding alternatives.

indicators.note: one piece filling another goes inside it
new suggests the letters of post are made into something fresh
in a down clue, turning up means writing the letters backwards

parts.note: No plus one, which is I as a Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Nobody applies for a newly created job, so the employer looks at other routes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turns up' reverses NOI to ION; 'new' rearranges POST to OPTS; 'to fill' puts ION inside to give OPT-ION-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Options are choices one may pick among, as are alternatives.

clue.text: Sound tax ?

definitions.meaning: to ring a bell slowly, as for a funeral
a charge levied for using a road or bridge

explanation.definitionFit: A bell may ring out slowly and solemnly, and a levy may be charged on a road or bridge.

clue.text: Outlaws musicians-both ways it appears

parts.note: a group of musicians is a band

indicators.note: the word it is written forwards and then backwards, so it reads the same both ways

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: Outlaws turn out to be musicians, whichever way you look at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Both ways' gives IT followed by TI. Banditti is the Italian-style plural of bandit.
explanation.definitionFit: Banditti are bandits, lawless robbers who live outside the protection of the law.

clue.text: Intimidating people for mistake — it's wrong in a way — upsetting

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it
in a down clue, upsetting turns the street abbreviation upside down, so it reads upwards

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a mistake is an error

indicators.note: wrong signals that the letters of it's are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for a mistake, admitting it was wrong in an upsetting way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong' turns ITS into IST; 'upsetting' reverses ST to TS; 'in' puts ERROR plus IST between T and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Terrorists use violence and fear to coerce, so they are people who intimidate.

clue.text: Drug-one taken before tea-break, after work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: breaking the word tea splits it up and rearranges its letters

explanation.surface: Someone takes a dose of medicine just before a tea break at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break' rearranges TEA to ATE; the clue's 'before' and 'after work' set I after OP and ahead of ATE.
explanation.definitionFit: An opiate is a narcotic derived from opium, a kind of drug.

clue.text: Where yachtsmen often appear overbearing

definitions.meaning: in the Solent, the strait off the Isle of Wight famous for sailing

explanation.walkthrough: The Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and mainland England, a famous yachting area.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it places sailors in the busy strait off southern England; joined, it means arrogantly disrespectful.

clue.text: Man's man, perhaps

parts.note: a man from the Isle of Man, an inhabitant of an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.walkthrough: 'Man's man' looks like a manly sort of chap, but Man is the Isle of Man, a self-governing island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A man living on the Isle of Man is an inhabitant of an island.

clue.text: Girl feels awkward in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A girl feels awkward playing a role in a show.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsa is a girl's name, so it can stand for a girl.

clue.text: Simple church tunes for use in the home ?

parts.note: simple means easy
airs are tunes or melodies

explanation.surface: A request for simple hymn tunes suitable for singing at home.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is furniture meant for use in the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Armchairs are comfortable household furniture, things found and used in a living room.

clue.text: Rifle this cathedral

definitions.meaning: a repeating rifle famous in the American West
a cathedral city in Hampshire, England

explanation.definitionFit: The name is both a famous lever-action firearm and an English city with a great medieval cathedral.

clue.text: Author of Kings

definitions.meaning: an American-born novelist who wrote The Turn of the Screw
two names borne by several English kings

explanation.walkthrough: England had eight kings called Henry and two called James.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist shares his two names with English monarchs, eight of one and two of the other.

clue.text: Artist viewed comparatively poorly by West End

parts.note: more poorly, that is more ill, is sicker

indicators.note: End points to the last letter of West

explanation.surface: A painter is thought less of by London's theatre district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End' looks like London's theatre district but is just the last letter of West. Walter Sickert was an English painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Walter Sickert was an English painter of the Camden Town Group, so an artist.

clue.text: Celestial ball

definitions.meaning: an old word for a person from China, once called the Celestial Empire
in cricket, a delivery from a left-arm wrist spinner that turns into a right-hander

explanation.walkthrough: China was once called the Celestial Empire, hence 'Celestial' for its people; cricket uses the term for a left-arm wrist-spin delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: The term is a dated, now offensive word for a Chinese person, and also a type of spin delivery in cricket.

clue.text: Records points with scores

parts.note: E and N are two compass points, east and north
in rugby a try is a score

explanation.surface: A scorer notes down the points and scores in a rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: Entries are items written into a register or log, so records.

clue.text: Othello character for poor Dr Roe-one attempt is enough

indicators.note: poor signals that the letters of Dr Roe are in a bad state, rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Poor Dr Roe needs only one try to land a part in Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor' rearranges DRROE to RODER. The printed grid answer ends ICO, but the wordplay and Shakespeare give Roderigo, Iago's dupe.
explanation.definitionFit: Roderigo is the foolish Venetian gentleman duped by Iago in Shakespeare's tragedy.

clue.text: American tie for the retired type

definitions.meaning: what Americans call a railroad tie, the beam supporting the rails
someone who has retired to bed

explanation.definitionFit: A railway beam under the track is called a tie in America, and one who has gone to bed is slumbering.

clue.text: For instance skipping it is easy

definitions.meaning: skipping with a rope is an example of a youngster's game
something no harder than a nursery game

explanation.definitionFit: Skipping is a typical game for youngsters, and the phrase also means a very simple task.

clue.text: Clobber the failures ?

definitions.meaning: British slang for clothes and gear
things or people that do not work out

explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' looks like a verb meaning hit, but it is British slang for clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are slang: clothing in one sense, flops in another.

clue.text: Translate poem to Yuletide?

indicators.note: the poem is added to the month, so it comes after

parts.note: Yuletide falls in December, abbreviated DEC
an ode is a poem

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a poem to be rendered into a Christmas verse.
explanation.definitionFit: To decode a message is to turn it into plain language, which is translating it.

clue.text: Tiny tot goes in yawning to see fabulous fountain

indicators.note: one piece going in another is put inside it

parts.note: agape means wide open, like a yawning mouth
a nip is a small drink, a tot

explanation.surface: A small child yawns and goes inside to see a fairy-tale fountain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tiny tot' looks like a toddler, but a tot is also a small measure of spirits, a NIP.
explanation.definitionFit: Aganippe was a spring on Mount Helicon sacred to the Muses in Greek myth, so a legendary fountain.

clue.text: Work up and down the deck

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read upwards and then downwards, so it is the same both ways

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work, written up and then down to give a palindrome

explanation.surface: A sailor labours up and down the ship's deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up and down' gives OP reversed, PO, followed by OP.
explanation.definitionFit: The poop is the raised deck at the stern of a ship.

clue.text: French statesman and Per sian leader act in opium combine

indicators.note: one piece set in another goes inside it
leader points to the first letter of Persian
combine says these letters are mixed together into a new order

parts.note: to act is to do

explanation.surface: A French politician and a Persian ruler join forces in an opium cartel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Combine' looks like a business cartel but is the anagram signal: P plus OPIUM gives POMPIU, and 'in' puts DO inside. Georges Pompidou was President of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Georges Pompidou was Prime Minister and then President of France, a French politician.

clue.text: Poor tailor in Venice

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of tailor are in a bad way, jumbled

explanation.surface: A tailor in Venice is down on his luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition names a place: the Rialto is the famous bridge and district in Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the famous bridge and market district on the Grand Canal in the city.

clue.text: Things they used to overlook in the trenches ?

definitions.text: Things they used to overlook in the trenches ?

parts.words: Things they used to overlook in the trenches
parts.note: soldiers in First World War trenches looked over the parapet using tube-and-mirror devices

explanation.definitionFit: These optical tubes with mirrors let a soldier see over a trench parapet without being exposed.
